story: Completing familiar fixed phrases and collocations, most often the 'uk' in '.co.uk' web addresses and ' course' in 'and, of course'.
Predicting the digit of a London postcode district (WC2, SE1, NW1, E2) right after the letter prefix at the end of a street address in a listing.

Predicting the next chunk of a multi-token proper name, most cleanly the start of a venue's website name after 'www.' where the venue was just named (Fabric -> www.fab..., Camden Passage -> www.cam...).
Predicting the full stop that ends a long descriptive guidebook sentence, after the final content word (a period the context has already seen many times).
Completing an all-caps word split across tokens, overwhelmingly the 'LE' of 'GOOGLE' in the recurring '( MAP GOOGLE MAP )' listing boilerplate (also MEDITERR-ANEAN, HOT-EL, LESBI-AN).
Predicting the pound sign before a price in a listing, or a famous place name in superlative phrases like 'one of England's / one of London's ...'.
Predicting the hyphen inside compound modifiers, especially after ordinals like '19th'/'20th' before 'century' (also eye-, snow-, three-storey style compounds).
Punctuation and word-piece continuations inside directory listings — the dot after a website's domain name, hyphens and commas in addresses — usually echoing a string already seen in the entry.
Predicting connective function words and commas that glue flowing guidebook prose together mid-sentence ('finest in the world', 'divides her time', 'grown its exhibition space by').
Predicting the newline immediately after an all-caps category tag (HOTEL, RUIN, CAFE, MUSEUM) or a section heading in the guidebook's listing layout.
Predicting the comma that continues an enumeration of items already underway ('urns, obelisks,', 'classical, opera,', 'omelettes, ploughman's lunches,').
Completing the second half of a split word or well-known compound ('stair-well', 'rose-mary', 'open-sand-wich', 'knick-kn-ack', 'Karl Marx').
Completing multi-token British place names, most often the possessive "'s" in King's Cross / King's Rd / Shepherd's Bush (also East-bourne, Port-obello, Pent-onville).
Predicting 'and' or '&' joining paired items, including the ampersand in guidebook section headings like 'Drinking & Nightlife' and 'Festivals & Events'.
